output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, Broadcom’s acquisition of VMware is complete: it closed on November 22, 2023, with VMware shareholders receiving approximately $30.788 billion in cash and 544 million Broadcom shares valued at $53.398 billion; the transaction was originally announced at about $61 billion, plus assumed VMware net debt. The merger terms allowed each VMware share to elect $142.50 in cash or 0.2520 Broadcom shares, prorated so roughly half the shares received each form of consideration, and Broadcom assumed $8.25 billion of VMware senior notes. Broadcom retained VMware’s core infrastructure-software business, while it sold VMware’s End-User Computing business to KKR for $3.5 billion on July 1, 2024; EU approval was conditional on 10-year interoperability and access commitments for competing Fibre Channel HBA suppliers.
caveats: The approximately $61 billion figure was the announced equity value in 2022; Broadcom’s later accounting reports separately disclose total purchase consideration of $86.290 billion and purchase consideration net of cash acquired of $79.648 billion, so these figures are not interchangeable.
The latest source opened for post-closing financial details is Broadcom’s fiscal-2025 Form 10-K, filed December 18, 2025; no later filing was used to assert a changed transaction structure.

passages.quote: On November 22, 2023, we acquired VMware, Inc. (“VMware”) in a cash-and-stock transaction (the “VMware Merger”). The VMware stockholders received approximately $30,788 million in cash and 544 million shares of Broadcom common stock with a fair value of $53,398 million.
passages.publisher: Broadcom Inc. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

passages.quote: Broadcom will acquire all of the outstanding shares of VMware in a cash-and-stock transaction that values VMware at approximately $61 billion. In addition, Broadcom will assume $8 billion of VMware net debt.

VMware shareholders will elect to receive either $142.50 in cash or 0.2520 shares of Broadcom common stock for each VMware share. The shareholder election will be subject to proration, resulting in approximately 50% of VMware’s shares being exchanged for cash consideration and 50% being exchanged for Broadcom common stock.
On July 1, 2024, we sold VMware’s end-user computing (“EUC”) business to KKR & Co. Inc. for cash consideration of $3.5 billion, after working capital adjustments.
passages.publisher: Broadcom Inc. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

passages.quote: The Commission's decision is conditional upon full compliance with the commitments, which will be in place for ten years.

output.question: What are the details of the VMware acquisition?

key_facts.fact: Broadcom completed the acquisition of VMware on November 22, 2023.
VMware shareholders received approximately $30.788 billion in cash and 544 million Broadcom shares valued at $53.398 billion.
The original transaction announcement valued the equity transaction at approximately $61 billion and said Broadcom would assume $8 billion of VMware net debt.
The merger consideration was $142.50 in cash or 0.2520 Broadcom shares per VMware share, subject to proration between the two forms.
Broadcom assumed $8.25 billion of VMware senior unsecured notes.
Broadcom sold VMware’s End-User Computing business to KKR for $3.5 billion on July 1, 2024.

The European Commission’s approval required 10-year commitments covering interoperability, access to APIs and technical support, source-code access, organizational separation, and monitoring for Fibre Channel HBA competition.
